item.title: Opioid Restitution Funds begin to reach local organizations
item.description: Funds from the Opioid Restitution Fund allocate $2 million dollars in community grants to 11 organizations across Baltimore by Mayor Brandon M. Scott to help to continue to mitigate the current crisis.

item.title: Brain tumor survivor reclaims her life, reshapes art and advocacy beyond disability
item.description: Zazel-Chavah O'Garra, a brain tumor survivor and former dancer, refuses to let her disability define her. She now works as a social worker and inspires others through her dance company for disabled adults.

item.title: Tempers flare between District’s mayoral frontrunners Kenyan McDuffie and Janeese Lewis George during Free D.C. candidate forum
item.description: Candidate forum in Washington, D.C. turns chaotic as mayoral and U.S. House delegate candidates clash over promises and special interests.

item.title: ‘There is a cost to telling the truth.’ But Georgia Fort is undeterred
item.description: Independent journalist Georgia Fort reflects on her arrest and the fight for press freedom, highlighting the vital role of Black media in holding America accountable.

item.title: Beauty empire builder, Black bank founder: Remembering Rose Morgan
item.description: Discover the remarkable story of Rose Meta Morgan, the pioneering entrepreneur who built a thriving Black beauty empire in Harlem and co-founded a bank.

item.title: Baltimore women who turned tragedy into transformation for West Baltimore
item.description: Baltimore women transform tragedy into change, becoming organizers and advocates in communities defined by hardship. Read their inspiring stories.

item.title: Maryland advances LEAD Act to protect youth who wander or elope
item.description: The LEAD Act in Maryland aims to reduce elopement risks for youth with autism and improve emergency response through training and resources.

item.title: A message to Anne Arundel County: An apology without repair isn’t complete
item.description: Discover the importance of following apologies with action in the journey of healing from the legacy of slavery. Read more in this thought-provoking article.

item.title: Northeast SARE Partnership Grant seeks proposals for innovative farming projects
item.description: Northeast SARE Partnership Grant program seeks innovative farming practices. Researchers, educators, and service providers can secure up to $30,000.

item.title: Commentary: Black Americans face higher risk for colon cancer. Here’s why screening matters.
item.description: Learn about the importance of colorectal cancer screening, especially for African Americans, as one woman shares her personal story and urges early detection.
